description: Overlay-guide deeplink vocabulary for Volt Assistant. Each deeplink below is executable by the admin app (see admin_app_dev/lib/src/app.dart, _handleChatDeepLink). Use get_guide_deeplinks to fetch this vocabulary and build guide steps/actions with real targets only.

tabs.name: analytics
tabs.description: Your day at a glance: gross sales, discounts, net sales, collection, prep cost, and profit. Tap a headline card to drill into detail.

tabs.name: orders
tabs.description: Live order feed; new orders appear instantly from tables, Facebook Messenger, and the restaurant's website. The + button builds a new order (dine-in, parcel, or delivery → pick items → send to the kitchen).

tabs.name: tables
tabs.description: (Waiter role) every table; tap a free table to seat guests and take their order.

tabs.name: stock
tabs.description: Inventory management: items, suppliers, stock-in, end-of-day stock count, and scan-to-stock.

tabs.name: menu
tabs.description: Menu management: add/edit items and categories, apply discounts, set the delivery charge. 'Scan menu card' imports a whole printed menu by photographing it.

tabs.name: reports
tabs.description: Download the performance report for any period: daily sales, orders, and per-item totals.

tabs.name: more
tabs.description: Settings: language, printer settings, staff management, audit log, sign out.

navSpots.description: highlight:nav.<tab> lights up a sidebar tab, e.g. highlight:nav.orders.

conventions: tab:<name> switches the sidebar tab (roles see different sets).
screen:<name> opens a full screen (staff, audit, stock-in, end-of-day stock count).
modal:<name> opens the discount or delivery-charge editor sheet.
highlight:<spot> lights up an exact element in the current screen.
Each step auto-navigates: its target deeplink executes before the step is shown. The user advances by tapping the highlighted element itself; the app never advances by itself.
Give every step a spot when an element exists to highlight — the spotlight points at the element the user must tap. A step with both target and spot navigates itself and then points at the element.
Target-only steps (no spot) are only for opening a destination the next step will highlight; they show a Continue button the user taps to move on.
If a step's destination must be opened first, combine it in the same step: target opens the destination and the spot lights up the exact element.
